name: Focus ring
definition: The visible outline drawn around the element that currently holds keyboard focus, showing where the next keypress will land.
useWhen: marking where keyboard focus is sitting right now
notes: Head term. The stage already draws annotation rings, so the demo must not confuse its own ring with the specimen's.

name: Focus visible
definition: A focus style shown only when focus arrived by keyboard or another non-pointer route, so a mouse click does not leave a ring behind.
useWhen: showing the ring to keyboard users but not to clickers

name: Focus order
definition: The sequence keyboard focus follows through a page, which should match reading order instead of source quirks or positive tabindex values.
useWhen: the path Tab takes through a whole page
notes: iframe: the subject is the document's own focus order, which a shadow root cannot honestly stage.

name: Tab stop
definition: One position in the tab sequence: a place the Tab key can reach, counted once even when the widget it belongs to holds many focusable parts.
useWhen: counting how many Tab presses a widget costs

name: Tabbable
definition: Reachable by the Tab key, as opposed to merely focusable: an element with tabindex of -1 can take focus from script but never from Tab.
useWhen: distinguishing script focus from Tab reachability

sources.title: Eric Eggert: Two different kinds of focusable UI elements

notes: Tail gold: the distinction people reach for and cannot name. Headword could also be 'Focusable but not tabbable'.

name: Roving tabindex
definition: A focus technique where only one item in a composite widget is tabbable at a time and arrow keys move that single tab stop between siblings.
useWhen: arrow keys move inside, Tab leaves the whole group
notes: Radix ships RovingFocusGroup and Angular CDK ships FocusKeyManager; neither URL was confirmed this sweep.

name: Active descendant
definition: A focus technique where DOM focus stays on a container or input and aria-activedescendant names which child is active, used when focus must not move.
useWhen: the typing field must keep focus while a list moves

name: Focus management
definition: Deliberately moving keyboard focus after a state change so the reader lands on the new content instead of at the top of the document.
useWhen: deciding where focus goes when the UI changes
notes: Merge candidate with the existing focus-trap entry; focus management is the umbrella, focus trap is one case.

name: Focus restoration
definition: Returning focus to the control that opened an overlay once it closes, so the reader resumes where they were rather than at the start of the page.
useWhen: an overlay closes and focus has to go somewhere
notes: Subsumes 'initial focus' (where focus goes when the overlay opens); canonicalize may want both under one entry.

name: Keyboard trap
definition: A defect where focus enters a region and cannot be moved out with the keyboard alone, stranding anyone who does not use a pointer.
useWhen: naming the bug where Tab cannot get back out
notes: Deliberate contrast with the existing focus-trap entry: same mechanism, one intended and escapable, one not.

name: Focus not obscured
definition: The requirement that a focused control is not completely hidden by sticky headers, footers, cookie bars, or chat widgets when it receives focus.
useWhen: the sticky header swallows the focused control

sources.title: W3C F110: sticky footer or header hiding focused elements

name: Focus appearance
definition: The size and contrast a focus indicator must reach to count as visible: enough area around the control, enough change against both the control and its background.
useWhen: judging whether a focus ring is strong enough

name: Selection follows focus
definition: A pattern where moving focus in a list or tablist immediately selects the item, as opposed to requiring a separate Enter or Space to commit.
useWhen: deciding if arrowing also picks, or only moves

name: Live region
definition: A container marked so assistive technology reads changes inside it without moving focus, used for messages that appear after an action.
useWhen: something must be spoken without stealing focus
notes: Absorbs the search query 'screen reader announcement', which is a head phrase but not a separate concept.

name: Politeness level
definition: The urgency setting on a live region: polite waits for a pause in speech, assertive interrupts whatever is being read.
useWhen: choosing whether an update may interrupt speech

name: Atomic live region
definition: A live region setting that makes assistive technology re-read the whole region when any part of it changes, instead of only the changed fragment.
useWhen: a partial update would be read out of context

name: Status message
definition: A change in content that reports progress, result, or state and must be announced without taking focus, such as a count of search results.
useWhen: reporting an outcome the reader did not navigate to

name: Landmark
definition: A named region role (banner, navigation, main, complementary, contentinfo, search) that lets assistive technology jump between the major parts of a page.
useWhen: naming the big regions so they can be jumped between

name: Accessible name
definition: The string assistive technology announces for a control, computed from label, aria-labelledby, aria-label, or its own content in a fixed order of precedence.
useWhen: asking what a control is actually called out loud

sources.title: APG: Providing Accessible Names and Descriptions

name: Accessible description
definition: Supplementary text announced after a control's name, carrying hint or error detail without becoming part of the name itself.
useWhen: extra detail that should follow the name, not replace it

sources.title: APG: Providing Accessible Names and Descriptions

name: Accessibility tree
definition: The parallel tree a browser derives from the DOM, holding the role, name, state, and value that assistive technology actually reads.
useWhen: talking about what AT sees rather than what renders

name: Alt text
definition: The text alternative that stands in for an image, written to serve the same purpose in the same context rather than to describe every detail.
useWhen: writing what an image says when it cannot be seen

name: Decorative image
definition: An image that carries no information and is given an empty alt attribute so assistive technology skips it entirely.
useWhen: the picture adds nothing a reader would miss

name: Long description
definition: An extended text alternative for a chart, diagram, or map, linked or referenced because a short alt string cannot carry the content.
useWhen: the image is data and one line will not do

name: Icon button label
definition: The accessible name given to a control that shows only an icon, supplied by visually hidden text or aria-label because there is no visible wording.
useWhen: a button is a glyph and nothing else

sources.title: APG: Providing Accessible Names and Descriptions

implementations.name: Screen reader text for icon-only buttons

notes: Merge candidate with accessible-name; kept separate because it is the concrete case people search for.

name: Touch target size
definition: The minimum area a control must offer a finger or imprecise pointer, measured on the activation region rather than the painted glyph.
useWhen: sizing something for a fingertip, not a cursor

name: Target spacing
definition: The exception that lets an undersized control pass when no other target falls inside a 24 pixel circle centred on it, trading size for clearance.
useWhen: small controls that cannot grow but can be separated

name: Touch target expansion
definition: Padding or a pseudo element that grows a control's hit area past its visible bounds, so a small icon still meets the minimum target.
useWhen: the icon must stay small but the target must not
notes: Tail gold: the invisible padded rectangle around a 16px icon has no agreed name outside React Native's hitSlop.

name: Pointer cancellation
definition: Activating a control on pointer release rather than press, so someone who lands on the wrong target can slide off and abort.
useWhen: letting a mis-press be taken back before release

name: Dragging alternative
definition: A second, non-dragging route to anything a drag can do, such as arrow keys or a move-to menu on a sortable list.
useWhen: a drag is the only way to perform an action

name: Pointer gestures
definition: Path based or multi finger gestures such as pinch, swipe, and draw, which need a single pointer equivalent to stay operable.
useWhen: a pinch or swipe is the only way in

name: Motion actuation
definition: Triggering a function by moving the device itself, such as shake to undo, which needs a plain control alternative and an off switch.
useWhen: the gesture is a shake or tilt of the device

name: Reduced motion
definition: A user preference asking interfaces to cut non-essential animation, honoured by shortening, cross fading, or removing movement rather than by doing nothing.
useWhen: the reader has asked the system for less movement
notes: Cross-category: arguably belongs to motion. Recorded here because the preference and its media query are accessibility vocabulary.

name: Reduced transparency
definition: A user preference asking for opaque surfaces instead of blur and translucency, honoured by swapping frosted layers for solid fills.
useWhen: frosted panels have to become solid on request

sources.title: MDN: Using media queries for accessibility

notes: Direct counterpart to the existing glassmorphism entry: the preference that turns the frost off.

name: Increased contrast
definition: A user preference for more contrast than a theme's default, honoured by strengthening borders, text, and state colours rather than by shifting hues.
useWhen: the system asks for a higher contrast version

sources.title: MDN: Using media queries for accessibility

name: Forced colors mode
definition: A mode where the operating system replaces the page palette with a small user chosen set, so borders, icons, and states must survive without author colours.
useWhen: the OS throws your palette away and keeps the layout

name: Contrast ratio
definition: The measured luminance ratio between two colours, the number contrast requirements are written in: 4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text.
useWhen: putting a number on legibility of text over a fill
notes: Cross-category with color; the enumeration for color may produce a duplicate.

name: Non-text contrast
definition: The contrast requirement that applies to the parts of a control that are not text: borders, icons, focus rings, and state indicators.
useWhen: the thing that must be seen is a border or icon

name: Large text threshold
definition: The size at which text counts as large for contrast purposes (about 18pt, or 14pt when bold) and its required ratio drops from 4.5:1 to 3:1.
useWhen: deciding which contrast number a heading owes
notes: Cross-category with typography.

name: APCA
definition: A newer contrast model that weights polarity, size, and weight instead of a single luminance ratio, drafted as a successor to the WCAG 2 formula.
useWhen: the 4.5:1 number disagrees with what you can read
notes: Cross-category with color. Implementation rows need a fresh sweep; none confirmed here.

name: Use of color
definition: The rule that colour must never be the only carrier of meaning, so a red field also needs an icon, wording, or shape change.
useWhen: the only difference between two states is hue

implementations.name: Use of color and color blindness

name: Reflow
definition: The requirement that content works in one column at 320 CSS pixels wide without two dimensional scrolling, which is 400 percent zoom on a desktop.
useWhen: checking a layout at heavy zoom, not just on phones
notes: iframe: the subject is the document viewport and its scroller, which a shadow root cannot stand in for.

name: Text spacing override
definition: Content must survive a reader forcing larger line height, letter spacing, word spacing, and paragraph spacing, without clipping or overlap.
useWhen: a user stylesheet loosens every spacing value

name: Resize text
definition: Text must scale to at least 200 percent without loss of content or function, which rules out fixed pixel heights around wrapping copy.
useWhen: the reader has enlarged text, not the whole page

aliases.name: text-only zoom vs full page zoom

name: Dynamic Type
definition: Apple's system setting for the reader's preferred text size, which layouts follow instead of pinning type to fixed point values.
useWhen: naming the platform text size setting on Apple devices

name: Error identification
definition: Naming the field that failed and saying what went wrong in text, rather than only outlining the input in red.
useWhen: telling a reader which field failed and why

name: Error summary
definition: A block at the top of a form listing every failed field as links, focused on submit so the reader hears the count and can jump to each one.
useWhen: a long form fails and the reader needs the whole list
notes: Cross-category: could sit under component or pattern; recorded here because its whole rationale is focus and announcement.

name: Label in name
definition: The rule that a control's accessible name must contain its visible label text, so speaking the visible words works in voice control.
useWhen: aria-label and the visible text disagree

name: Placeholder as label
definition: The antipattern of using placeholder text as a field's only label, which vanishes on typing and usually fails both contrast and naming.
useWhen: naming why a placeholder-only field is broken

name: Label association
definition: The programmatic link between a label and its field, made by for and id or by wrapping, which makes the label clickable and the field named.
useWhen: connecting the words to the input they name
notes: SPEC section 8 warns that a choreography cannot rely on a label's native activation, which makes this a careful demo.

name: Input purpose
definition: Machine readable autocomplete tokens on personal fields, which let browsers autofill and let personalisation tools add familiar icons or wording.
useWhen: telling the browser what a field is actually for

name: Accessible authentication
definition: A sign-in route that never requires a cognitive function test such as recalling a password or solving a puzzle without offering an alternative.
useWhen: a login demands memory or puzzle solving

name: Redundant entry
definition: The rule against asking for the same information twice in one process, unless it is re-entered for a real reason such as confirmation.
useWhen: a wizard asks for the address a second time

name: Timeout warning
definition: A warning before a session or form expires with a simple way to extend it, so a slower reader does not lose their work silently.
useWhen: a session is about to expire under the reader
notes: Cross-category: could equally be a pattern entry.

name: Pause, stop, hide
definition: A visible control for content that moves, blinks, scrolls, or updates on its own, so a reader can stop it before reading around it.
useWhen: something animates or refreshes without being asked

name: Flashing content
definition: Content that flashes more than three times per second in a large enough area, restricted because it can trigger seizures.
useWhen: judging whether a flash rate is dangerous

aliases.name: general flash and red flash thresholds

sources.title: WCAG 2.2: Three Flashes or Below Threshold

notes: demo: none on purpose. Building a specimen that flashes would be the harm the term names.

name: Character key shortcuts
definition: Single letter shortcuts that fire without a modifier, which must be switchable off or remappable because speech input and screen readers trigger them by accident.
useWhen: a bare letter key does something on the page

name: Access key
definition: An author assigned shortcut key for a control, historically shown as an underlined letter, unreliable because it collides with browser and screen reader keys.
useWhen: naming the underlined mnemonic letter in a control

name: Inert
definition: A state that removes a subtree from focus order, hit testing, and the accessibility tree at once, used to seal the background behind a dialog.
useWhen: making a whole region unreachable, not just invisible
notes: Clean contrast with the existing aria-hidden and focus-trap entries: inert does all three jobs at once.

name: Heading hierarchy
definition: The nested outline formed by heading levels, navigated directly by assistive technology and broken by skipping a level or picking a level for its size.
useWhen: structuring a page so it can be skimmed by heading

name: Reading order
definition: The order content is exposed in the DOM, which drives both speech output and tab order, and which visual reordering can silently contradict.
useWhen: the visual order and the source order disagree

name: Screen reader
definition: Software that speaks or brailles the accessibility tree and supplies its own keyboard commands for moving through a page.
useWhen: naming the software that reads an interface aloud

name: Browse mode
definition: The screen reader mode that intercepts keystrokes for reading and navigation, as opposed to focus or forms mode where keys reach the page.
useWhen: explaining why a key press never reached your widget

sources.title: Accessibility Developer Guide: Browse and focus modes
Tink: Understanding screen reader interaction modes

notes: Tail gold. Absorbs 'virtual cursor' as an alias rather than a separate entry.

name: Rotor
definition: VoiceOver's dial for choosing what a swipe or flick moves between: headings, links, landmarks, form controls, or characters.
useWhen: naming the VoiceOver dial that picks a navigation unit

sources.title: Apple Support: Use the VoiceOver rotor on Mac

name: Switch access
definition: Operating a device with one or two switches, where a scanning cursor steps through targets in turn and a press selects the highlighted one.
useWhen: input is a single button and time, not a pointer

name: Voice control
definition: Operating an interface by speaking control names or numbered overlays, which makes the visible wording of a control its address.
useWhen: the reader clicks by saying the button's name

name: Braille display
definition: A refreshable braille row that renders the same accessibility tree as speech, with abbreviated role names authors can override.
useWhen: output is a braille line, not synthesized speech

name: Captions
definition: Synchronised text for a video's audio, including speaker changes and meaningful sound, distinct from subtitles which only translate dialogue.
useWhen: text that carries the sound of a video, not a translation
notes: Slug avoids colliding with a typography 'caption' (figure caption); canonicalize should keep both apart.

name: Audio description
definition: A narration track describing visual information the soundtrack leaves out, fitted into the gaps between dialogue.
useWhen: the picture carries information the audio does not

name: Transcript
definition: A full text version of time based media, readable without playing it and searchable by both people and machines.
useWhen: offering the whole of a video or podcast as text

sources.title: WebAIM: Captions, Transcripts, and Audio Descriptions

name: Link purpose
definition: Whether a link's own text says where it goes, the reason a list of read more and click here links fails when read out of context.
useWhen: judging link text pulled out of its sentence

name: Current page indicator
definition: The marking of which item in a navigation set is the one you are on, exposed with aria-current so it survives without the colour cue.
useWhen: showing which nav item is the page you are on

name: Pressed state
definition: The on or off state of a toggle button, exposed with aria-pressed so the control reads as sticky rather than as a plain button.
useWhen: a button stays down after you press it

name: Expanded state
definition: The open or closed state of a disclosure, exposed with aria-expanded on the control that owns it rather than on the panel it reveals.
useWhen: the trigger must say whether its panel is open

name: Mixed state checkbox
definition: A checkbox showing a third, indeterminate state when only some of the boxes it governs are checked.
useWhen: a parent box stands over a partly checked group
notes: Cross-category: reads as a component to most people; recorded here because the third state exists for the semantics.

name: Focusable disabled
definition: A control styled as unavailable but left in the tab order with aria-disabled, so a reader can find it and learn why it is off.
useWhen: a disabled control still needs to be discoverable
notes: Tail gold: the trade-off between the native disabled attribute and aria-disabled has no popular name.

name: Invalid state
definition: The programmatic mark that a field's value failed validation, paired with a pointer to the message that explains it.
useWhen: the field itself must report that it is wrong

name: Role description
definition: An author supplied name for a widget's role, spoken in place of the stock role name, which overrides the platform wording and misleads easily.
useWhen: renaming what a widget calls itself out loud

name: Header association
definition: The markup that ties a data cell to its row and column headers, so a cell read on its own still says what it is.
useWhen: a table cell must announce which column it is in

name: Hoverable, dismissible, persistent
definition: The three conditions content revealed on hover or focus must meet: reachable with the pointer, dismissible without moving focus, and not self-closing.
useWhen: judging whether a tooltip or flyout behaves

sources.title: WCAG 2.2: Content on Hover or Focus

notes: Tail gold: the trio is always cited together and has no single popular headword.

name: Sensory characteristics
definition: Instructions that lean on shape, size, position, or sound alone, such as the round button on the right, which fail when those cues are not perceived.
useWhen: copy points at a control by shape or position

name: Route announcement
definition: Telling assistive technology that a client side navigation happened, by moving focus to the new heading or posting the new title to a live region.
useWhen: the URL changed but the page never reloaded

sources.title: Dave Rupert: Accessible page navigation in single page apps

notes: iframe: the subject is the document title and the document's focus, so it needs its own document.

name: Consistent help
definition: Keeping the same help route, a contact link, a chat launcher, a self-help pane, in the same relative place on every page so a stuck reader can find it again.
useWhen: placing the help affordance so it never moves
notes: WCAG 2.2 addition (3.2.6). The demo can show two pages of one flow with the help control anchored versus wandering.

name: Change of context
definition: A shift big enough to disorient a reader, a new page, a new window, a moved focus, a rearranged form, and the rule that it should follow a request rather than a keystroke.
useWhen: naming the surprise a select or focus event should not cause

name: Page title
definition: The document title, the first thing a screen reader speaks and the only label a reader has when picking between tabs, windows, and history entries.
useWhen: the label a page carries outside its own viewport
notes: iframe: the subject is the document title, which only exists at document scope.

name: Language attribute
definition: The declared language of a document or a passage inside it, which picks the voice, the pronunciation rules, and the hyphenation a reader gets.
useWhen: a quoted passage is in another language than the page
notes: iframe: the page language lives on the root element of a document.

name: Images of text
definition: Text baked into a raster image, which cannot be resized, restyled, selected, translated, or read by anything but the alt attribute someone remembered to write.
useWhen: arguing a headline should be text, not a picture of text

name: Audio control
definition: A way to stop sound that started on its own, because autoplaying audio drowns out the screen reader voice a reader depends on to find the control that stops it.
useWhen: anything makes noise before the reader asked

name: Sign language interpretation
definition: A signed track alongside video, presented as an inset or a companion stream, for readers whose first language is a sign language rather than the written caption text.
useWhen: captions are not the reader first language

name: Name, role, value
definition: The three things every control has to expose to assistive technology: what it is called, what kind of thing it is, and what state it is currently in.
useWhen: auditing whether a custom control is really a control

name: Semantic HTML
definition: Reaching for the element that already means what you mean, so name, role, keyboard behaviour, and platform conventions arrive for free instead of being rebuilt.
useWhen: choosing between a native element and a rebuilt one

name: First rule of ARIA
definition: The maxim that no ARIA is better than bad ARIA: if a native element does the job, use it rather than pinning a role onto a div and reimplementing the behaviour.
useWhen: someone proposes a role instead of an element

aliases.name: no ARIA is better than bad ARIA

sources.title: W3C: Using ARIA, rules of ARIA use
Primer: The first rule of ARIA

name: Button versus link
definition: The rule that decides which element to use: a link goes somewhere, a button does something, and the choice sets the keyboard, the cursor, and the announced role.
useWhen: a control looks like a button but navigates

name: POUR
definition: The four principles WCAG is built on, perceivable, operable, understandable, and robust, used as a shorthand for sorting an accessibility problem into a bucket.
useWhen: classifying what kind of barrier you are looking at
notes: Vocabulary rather than an interface part; demo: none unless canonicalize finds a way to show it.

name: Conformance level
definition: The A, AA, or AAA tier a success criterion sits in, and the tier a product claims, which is what people mean when they say a design is "AA".
useWhen: someone says the target is AA and you need the tiers

implementations.name: WCAG AA across all standard themes

name: Plain language
definition: Writing interface copy at the reading level of the people using it, with short sentences, familiar words, and the point first, rather than at the level of the org chart.
useWhen: the copy is correct but nobody can act on it

name: Abbreviation expansion
definition: Giving the full form of an acronym or initialism on first use or on demand, so a reader who does not already know it is not left guessing.
useWhen: an interface is full of internal initialisms

name: Pronunciation
definition: How a synthetic voice says a word, and the hints an author can give when the default reading turns a product name, a units string, or a homograph into nonsense.
useWhen: the screen reader mangles a name or a number
notes: Audible only, so a visual demo can at best show the markup and a transcript of what is spoken.

name: Orientation lock
definition: Restricting a screen to portrait or landscape, which strands anyone whose device is fixed in a mount or a wheelchair arm in the orientation the design refused.
useWhen: a layout only works one way up

name: Consistent identification
definition: Calling the same function by the same name and icon everywhere in a product, so a reader who learned it once does not have to relearn it per screen.
useWhen: the same action has three names across screens

name: Presentation role
definition: Stripping an element of its semantics while leaving it on screen, so a table used for layout or a list used for spacing stops being announced as one.
useWhen: markup you needed for layout is lying about meaning
notes: Distinct from aria-hidden: presentation keeps the element and its content readable, it only drops the role.

name: Presentational children
definition: The rule that some roles flatten everything inside them into their own label, which is why an icon and a span inside a button are never announced separately.
useWhen: markup inside a control vanishes from the a11y tree

name: Owned element
definition: A child the accessibility tree is told to adopt from elsewhere in the DOM, used when the visual nesting a role requires is impossible in the markup.
useWhen: a listbox and its options cannot be nested in markup
notes: Support is patchy and it is easy to build a tree nobody can navigate, so canonicalize may want the cautionary framing.

name: Busy state
definition: Marking a region as still loading so assistive technology waits for the finished result instead of reading each row as it streams in.
useWhen: a region updates in pieces and each piece speaks

name: Sort state
definition: The announced direction of the one column a table is currently sorted by, carried on that column header alone rather than on every sortable header.
useWhen: a sorted column shows an arrow but says nothing

name: Set size and position
definition: Telling assistive technology how big a list really is and where an item sits in it, so a windowed or paginated list still announces "item 6 of 16".
useWhen: only twenty rows of ten thousand are in the DOM

name: Has popup
definition: A hint on a trigger that says something will open and what kind of thing it will be, a menu, a listbox, a dialog, before the reader commits to pressing it.
useWhen: a button opens a menu and gives no warning

name: Group label
definition: The one name that covers a set of controls, a question above its radio buttons or a heading above an address block, so each field is heard in context.
useWhen: individual field labels make no sense on their own
notes: Overlaps the component-category fieldset record: this one is about the name, that one about the box.

name: Required field indicator
definition: How a form says a field cannot be left empty, in the label text, in the announced name, and not by an asterisk whose meaning is explained somewhere else.
useWhen: deciding how to mark required versus optional fields

name: Positive tabindex
definition: Using tabindex values above zero to force an order, which yanks those elements to the front of the whole page sequence and is almost always a bug.
useWhen: someone proposes tabindex="1" to fix an order
notes: Antipattern term. Verify the MDN URL before publishing: the global-attributes path moved with the Reference reshuffle.

name: Initial focus
definition: Where focus lands when a view, dialog, or page first appears, chosen deliberately rather than left on the body or dumped on the first close button.
useWhen: a dialog opens and nobody decided where focus goes

name: Focus guard
definition: A hidden sentinel element placed at the edge of a trapped region, there to catch focus leaving it and bounce it back without relying on keydown interception.
useWhen: building a trap that survives browser chrome and iframes

name: Reading flow
definition: A CSS property that repoints reading and tab order at the visual arrangement of a flex or grid container, instead of leaving both stuck in source order.
useWhen: a visual reorder has left tab order zigzagging
notes: Experimental and Chromium-only as of this sweep, which makes it a good tail term rather than guidance.

name: Spatial navigation
definition: Moving focus by direction rather than by sequence, so arrow keys, a D-pad, or a TV remote jump to the nearest control up, down, left, or right.
useWhen: the input is a remote or a game pad, not a keyboard

name: Inverted colors
definition: A whole-screen colour inversion applied by the OS, which flips a design nobody tested upside down and turns every shadow into a highlight.
useWhen: the OS inverts your palette and shadows go wrong

name: Screen curtain
definition: A screen reader mode that switches the display off entirely while navigation keeps working, used for privacy and by sighted testers to check an audio-only run.
useWhen: testing whether a flow works with the screen dark

sources.title: Apple Support: Use Screen Curtain with VoiceOver

notes: Not renderable as a specimen; a candidate for a term with no demo, or a staged illustration.

name: Review cursor
definition: A second cursor a screen reader user can move over the screen to read text without moving the system focus, so inspecting a region does not disturb the app.
useWhen: a reader inspects content without leaving the field

name: Explore by touch
definition: The touch screen reader mode where dragging a finger reads whatever is under it and activation takes a second, deliberate tap, so nothing fires by accident.
useWhen: designing touch targets a finger has to find blind

sources.title: Android Accessibility Help: Navigate your device with TalkBack

name: Verbosity
definition: How much a screen reader says about each thing it reaches, a user setting that decides whether your carefully written description is heard at all.
useWhen: arguing about how much detail a label should carry

name: Accessibility overlay
definition: A third party script bolted onto a site with a promise of automatic compliance, usually a floating widget of font and contrast toggles that fixes nothing underneath.
useWhen: someone proposes buying a widget instead of fixing
notes: Contested term with a strong consensus against the products; the entry should carry that consensus rather than stay neutral.

name: Curb cut effect
definition: The pattern where something built for a disabled minority turns out to serve everyone, the way dropped kerbs serve prams and captions serve noisy rooms.
useWhen: justifying accessibility work to a sceptical room

aliases.name: solve for one extend to many

name: Situational disability
definition: A barrier that comes from the moment rather than the body, one arm holding a baby, sunlight on a screen, a noisy train, and that makes the audience for access everyone.
useWhen: widening who a barrier actually affects

name: Accessibility annotation
definition: Notes attached to a design file that spell out the things a mockup cannot show: heading levels, focus order, names, roles, live regions, and alt text.
useWhen: handing a design over without losing the semantics

name: Magic tap
definition: A screen reader gesture that fires the one action a screen is most likely about, answering the call or pausing the track, without the reader hunting for the control.
useWhen: a screen has one obvious action worth a shortcut

sources.title: Apple: Supporting Accessibility (View Controller Programming Guide)

name: Escape gesture
definition: The screen reader equivalent of the Escape key, a two finger scrub that dismisses a sheet or steps back a level and that a custom overlay has to answer for itself.
useWhen: a custom sheet ignores the platform dismiss gesture

sources.title: Apple: Supporting Accessibility (View Controller Programming Guide)

name: Functional need
definition: A statement of the gap between what a person can do and what a design demands, used by the WCAG 3 draft in place of sorting people into disability categories.
useWhen: framing a barrier without naming a diagnosis
notes: WCAG 3 draft vocabulary, still moving. Worth a record because audits already use the phrase.

name: Screen magnification
definition: Blowing part of the screen up many times over, so a reader sees a keyhole of the layout at a time and anything far from the action is effectively off screen.
useWhen: a toast at the corner will never be seen
notes: Explains why feedback belongs near the control that caused it rather than in a screen corner.

name: Double speak
definition: A control announced twice because its name arrives from two places at once, typically an aria-label stacked on visible text or a title repeating the label.
useWhen: a screen reader says the same thing twice

sources.title: W3C public-aria: Does double announced content bother screen reader users?

name: Nested interactive
definition: A focusable control placed inside another control, such as a button inside a link or a checkbox inside a row that is itself clickable, which leaves an unreachable tab stop.
useWhen: a whole card is clickable and so is its button

aliases.name: interactive controls must not be nested

sources.title: Deque: Interactive controls must not be nested

name: Focusable scroll region
definition: Giving a scrollable box its own tab stop so a keyboard user can scroll it, which matters whenever the content inside holds no focusable element of its own.
useWhen: a code block or log pane scrolls but cannot be reached

sources.title: Deque: Scrollable region must have keyboard access

name: Hidden but focusable
definition: An element hidden from assistive technology that is still in the tab sequence, so keyboard focus lands on something a screen reader refuses to describe.
useWhen: focus disappears into an offscreen or hidden panel

sources.title: W3C ACT: Element with aria-hidden has no content in sequential focus navigation
Deque: aria-hidden elements do not contain focusable elements

name: Symbol support
definition: Marking a control with a concept code so a reader who uses an augmentative symbol set sees their own familiar picture in place of your icon and wording.
useWhen: the words and icons themselves are the barrier
notes: Cognitive accessibility vocabulary, still a draft spec, but the only name for the idea.

name: Line focus
definition: A reading aid that dims everything except one to five lines of text, so the eye has a single band to track and cannot skip or reread a line by accident.
useWhen: long prose has to be readable line by line

sources.title: Microsoft Support: Use Immersive Reader in Microsoft Edge

name: Reader mode
definition: A browser view that throws away your layout and rebuilds the article as plain text the reader can restyle, which is a verdict on how readable the original was.
useWhen: checking what survives when the design is stripped

sources.title: Microsoft Support: Use Immersive Reader and reading mode in Microsoft Edge

notes: Depends entirely on semantic markup, so the demo can show a page that reader mode empties.

name: Read aloud
definition: Speaking page text with synthetic voice for readers who are not blind, with word highlighting as it goes, which is a reading aid rather than a screen reader.
useWhen: distinguishing text to speech from a screen reader

sources.title: Microsoft Support: Use Immersive Reader in Microsoft Edge

name: Sonification
definition: Turning data into sound, mapping a series to pitch or rhythm, so a chart can be heard as a shape rather than described one value at a time.
useWhen: a chart has to be perceivable without sight

sources.title: University of Washington: Making data visualizations accessible

name: Accessibility trait
definition: The platform flag on a native view that says what it is and how it behaves, the mobile counterpart to a role plus a state, and the thing a custom control has to set by hand.
useWhen: a custom native control announces as plain text

sources.title: Deque: What iOS traits actually do
Mobile A11y: iOS UIKit accessibility traits

name: Accessibility grouping
definition: Collapsing a cluster of elements, an icon plus a label plus a value, into one thing assistive technology stops at, instead of three stops that mean nothing apart.
useWhen: a card reads as five fragments instead of one item

name: Focus delegation
definition: A shadow root option that forwards focus from the host into the first focusable element inside it, so clicking the padding of a custom element does not leave focus nowhere.
useWhen: a custom element swallows clicks near its edges

sources.title: Frontend Masters: Shadow DOM focus delegation

notes: Directly relevant to this project: every specimen in shadow mode is a host whose focus behaviour this decides.

name: Streaming announcement
definition: How a screen reader is told about text that arrives token by token, holding the region quiet while it streams and speaking once when the answer is complete.
useWhen: a reply types itself in and floods the announcer

sources.title: Harvard User Research Center: Review of generative AI chatbots accessibility

notes: Emerging vocabulary, and one of the few places where aria-busy earns its keep.

name: ARIA notify
definition: A proposed API for speaking a message directly to assistive technology, without the live region trick of mutating hidden text and hoping the timing works out.
useWhen: an announcement has no element it belongs to
notes: Proposal stage. Worth a record because live-region workarounds are usually explained by contrast with it.

name: Cognitive load
definition: The mental effort an interface demands, split between the work the task really needs and the work the design added by way of clutter, jargon, and avoidable steps.
useWhen: a screen is correct but exhausting to use

sources.title: W3C WAI: Cognitive Accessibility at W3C

notes: Sits on the border with the pattern category; nothing in the other files claims it, so it is filed here with its cognitive accessibility framing.

name: Chunking
definition: Breaking content into small labelled pieces, short paragraphs, lists, and headings, so a reader can hold one piece at a time instead of the whole wall.
useWhen: a dense block has to be read by anyone tired

sources.title: W3C: Keep Text Succinct (cognitive accessibility design pattern)

notes: Overlaps typography and content design; filed here because the cited pattern is cognitive accessibility guidance.
